patients.summary: Construction worker and current smoker with COPD who joined in 2020; a 2022 low-dose CT found a small right lower lobe nodule, and in 2024 a right upper lobe mass proved to be stage IIIA non-small cell lung cancer treated with chemoradiation and durvalumab. Last seen 2025-05-09; outside records then show a COPD admission in 2025 and progression with SIADH in 2026, now on docetaxel.

documents.title: New Patient Visit
documents.author: PCP
documents.body:
43M, framer/carpenter on commercial crews, coming over from his old primary care office because his coworker is a member here and he wanted to be able to text a doctor. Came in at 7:30 so he could get to the site by 9.

COPD: told about two years ago by his last doctor after he got winded on ladders; did a breathing test then. On tiotropium capsule every morning and albuterol, uses the rescue maybe 2-3x a week, more in humid weather or around drywall dust. No ED visits, no steroid bursts he can remember. Mild morning cough, clear phlegm.

Tobacco: started at around 17, a pack and a half most days for years, now about a pack. Roughly 30 pack-years. Has tried cold turkey twice. Not interested in a quit date right now - 'it's the only break I get on the job.'
Alcohol: a few beers on weekends, not every weekend. No drugs.

PMH: COPD. PSH: none. Allergies: none known.
Family: father with COPD. Paternal uncle had lung cancer. No other family history he knows of.
Social: single, lives in Ludlow. Construction worker.

Meds: tiotropium 18 mcg inhaled daily, albuterol HFA 1-2 puffs q4-6h prn.

Exam: well appearing, talks in full sentences. HEENT unremarkable. Neck supple, no nodes. Lungs: good air movement, no wheeze, no crackles. Heart regular, no murmur. Abd soft. Ext: no clubbing, no edema. Skin: no lesions of concern.

A/P
1. COPD, on LAMA, symptoms controlled. Continue tiotropium and albuterol. Will get old records including his spirometry.
2. Tobacco use disorder. Advised quitting, offered patch/varenicline and quitline. Declined for now. Will revisit.
3. Health maintenance: CMP, CBC, lipids, A1c, one-time hep C and HIV screen drawn today. Flu shot when the vaccine arrives.
RTC for physical in spring, sooner as needed. Records release signed.

orders.reason: Heavy smoker with COPD, shared decision

documents.title: Annual Physical
documents.author: PCP
documents.body:
45M here for his physical. Feels fine, no complaints, but he has something on his mind: a buddy of his, 52, who smoked about the way Derek does, was just diagnosed with lung cancer. Wants to know straight up how much more likely he is to get it than someone who never smoked.

Breathing: same as last year. Albuterol a few times a week. No exacerbations. No cough change, no hemoptysis, no weight loss, no night sweats.
Tobacco: still about a pack a day, roughly 30 pack-years.
Family: father COPD. No parent or sibling with cancer; a paternal uncle had lung cancer.

Meds: tiotropium 18 mcg daily, albuterol prn. Allergies: none known.

Vitals: BP 130/85, HR 78, RR 16.
Exam: unremarkable. Lungs without wheeze or crackles, heart regular, abdomen benign, no clubbing, no edema, no adenopathy.

A/P
1. Lung cancer risk. Long talk. Told him plainly that heavy smoking raises lung cancer risk many times over compared with never-smokers, that the risk keeps climbing with each pack-year, and that quitting is the single thing that lowers it. He asked about a CT scan like his friend had. The screening guideline starts at 50 and he is 45; we went over what a CT can and can't do, false alarms, radiation. Given his ~30 pack-years, COPD and his uncle, we agreed to do a low-dose CT now - understanding he's under the usual age and insurance may push back. Ordered; will send prior auth.
2. Tobacco: he says this scare has him thinking. Not ready for medication yet. Will message me if he wants to start.
3. COPD: stable, continue.
4. Colorectal screening: 45 now - FIT kit given.
5. Labs today.
RTC 1 year, sooner as needed.

reports.study: Low-dose CT chest for lung cancer screening
reports.text:
TECHNIQUE: Low-dose helical CT of the chest without intravenous contrast.
COMPARISON: None.
FINDINGS: Lungs: 6 mm solid non-calcified nodule in the right lower lobe (mean diameter on lung windows). No other pulmonary nodules. No consolidation. Airways are patent. Pleura: no effusion or pneumothorax. Mediastinum and hila: no lymphadenopathy. Heart normal in size; no pericardial effusion. Visualized upper abdomen unremarkable. Bones: no aggressive lesion.
reports.conclusion: 6 mm solid right lower lobe nodule. Lung-RADS 3, probably benign. Recommend 6-month low-dose CT.

documents.title: Low-dose CT chest

orders.reason: 6 mm RLL nodule in heavy smoker with COPD

documents.title: CT result call
documents.author: PCP
documents.body: Called him on his lunch break. CT shows a single 6 mm nodule in the right lower lung. Explained that most spots this size are not cancer, that the radiologist's category means a repeat scan in about 6 months, and that given his history I'd like a lung specialist to see him and own the follow-up. He was quiet, then asked if he should quit now. Yes. Pulmonology referral placed, marked soon.

documents.title: Pulmonology consultation
documents.author: pulmonology
documents.body:
PULMONARY MEDICINE - OUTPATIENT CONSULTATION
Date of visit: 09/28/2022
Referred by: primary care, for a pulmonary nodule.

Mr. Plante is a 45-year-old construction worker with COPD on tiotropium and an active smoking history of about 30 pack-years. In March he talked with his PCP about his lung cancer risk after a friend was diagnosed, and a low-dose CT on 09/12/2022 showed a 6 mm solid, non-calcified right lower lobe nodule. He has no symptoms today. He is anxious and wants to know the odds that this is cancer.

Meds: tiotropium 18 mcg inhaled daily; albuterol HFA as needed.
Allergies: none known.
Family history: father with COPD; paternal uncle with lung cancer.
Social: current smoker, about 30 pack-years. Occasional alcohol.

Exam: comfortable, no distress. Lungs clear without wheeze. Cardiac regular. No clubbing or adenopathy.

Imaging reviewed: single 6 mm solid nodule, right lower lobe, smooth. No adenopathy.

Impression:
1. Solitary pulmonary nodule, 6 mm, right lower lobe. I explained that how likely a nodule is to be cancer depends on the person screened as much as the scan - his age, his smoking history and the size and shape of the nodule all go into it. Most nodules this size turn out to be benign, but with his exposure I consider this one concerning and want it watched closely.
2. COPD, stable on LAMA.
3. Tobacco use - cessation strongly advised.

Plan: repeat low-dose CT chest in 6 months. Return after that scan. Continue current inhalers.

cc: primary care

documents.title: Office Visit - cough, weight loss
documents.author: PCP
documents.body:
S: Texted Friday asking to come in. Dry cough for about 3 months, not his usual morning cough - comes on through the day, no phlegm. Has lost about 15 lb without trying; belt is two notches tighter. Appetite a bit down. No fever, no night sweats, no blood in what he coughs up. Breathing about baseline otherwise. Still smoking.

O: Weight 77.2 kg, down from 84 at his physical in April. Vitals otherwise as charted, afebrile. Appears well, not in distress. Lungs: breath sounds decreased over the right upper chest; no wheeze, no crackles. Heart regular. No supraclavicular or cervical nodes. No clubbing.

A/P
Persistent cough and unintentional weight loss in a ~30 pack-year smoker with COPD and a known RLL nodule (pulmonology wanted a repeat CT in 2023). Worried about this. Chest x-ray today; urgent pulmonology referral placed and I called their office directly to get him in this month. Told him honestly why I'm moving fast. He'll text me with anything new.

documents.title: Pulmonology follow-up
documents.author: pulmonology
documents.body:
PULMONARY MEDICINE - OFFICE NOTE
Date of visit: 09/27/2024

Seen in 2022 for a 6 mm right lower lobe nodule. Now referred back urgently by primary care: three months of a new dry cough and an unintended 15 lb weight loss. Denies fevers, night sweats or hemoptysis. Still smoking, cutting down since last week. COPD on tiotropium, albuterol as needed.

Family history: father with COPD; paternal uncle with lung cancer.
Social: construction worker. Current smoker, 30 pack-years. Drinks occasionally.
Allergies: none known.

Exam: afebrile. BP 130/85, HR 78, RR 16. Thin, comfortable. Decreased breath sounds over the right upper lobe. No wheeze. No palpable adenopathy.

Data: CBC - Hgb 14 g/dL, WBC 7,000, platelets 250,000. Na 140, K 4.2, creatinine 1.0, glucose 95.
Chest x-ray 9/17 (reviewed): right upper lobe mass.

Assessment: right upper lobe mass with weight loss in a heavy smoker - suspicious for primary lung cancer.
Plan:
1. CT chest with contrast this week.
2. Bronchoscopy with endobronchial ultrasound for tissue and nodal sampling, depending on CT.
3. He understands the concern. Strongly encouraged to stop smoking.

cc: primary care

reports.text:
TECHNIQUE: CT of the chest with intravenous contrast.
COMPARISON: Low-dose CT 09/12/2022; chest radiograph 09/17/2024.
FINDINGS: There is a 4.0 cm mass in the right upper lobe. Mediastinal lymphadenopathy is present. The previously described 6 mm solid nodule in the right lower lobe is unchanged. No pleural effusion. No pericardial effusion. Heart size normal. Visualized upper abdomen unremarkable. No destructive osseous lesion.
reports.conclusion: 4 cm right upper lobe mass with mediastinal lymphadenopathy, highly suspicious for primary lung malignancy. Stable 6 mm right lower lobe nodule.

documents.title: CT chest with contrast
documents.author: radiology
documents.body: Report received from the outside imaging center. 4 cm RUL mass with mediastinal adenopathy; RLL 6 mm nodule unchanged since 2022. Routed to PCP; pulmonology also copied.

documents.title: CT reviewed
documents.author: PCP
documents.body: Reviewed CT. Spoke with pulmonology - bronchoscopy with EBUS booked for 10/9. Called Derek and went over it. He asked whether this is the spot from 2022 - no, that one hasn't changed; this is in the upper lobe.

documents.title: Bronchoscopy with endobronchial ultrasound
documents.author: pulmonology
documents.body:
PROCEDURE REPORT - received 10/10/2024
Date of procedure: 10/09/2024
Procedure: flexible bronchoscopy with endobronchial ultrasound-guided transbronchial needle aspiration of the right upper lobe mass and mediastinal lymph nodes.
Indication: 4 cm right upper lobe mass with mediastinal lymphadenopathy.
Anesthesia: moderate sedation, oral route.
Findings: airways without endobronchial lesion. Enlarged mediastinal nodes visualized by EBUS and sampled; the mass was sampled as well. Rapid on-site evaluation showed malignant cells.
Complications: none. Minimal bleeding.
Disposition: discharged home with his sister. Final pathology to follow.

conditions.label: Malignant neoplasm of lung
conditions.note: Non-small cell carcinoma, right upper lobe, mediastinal nodes involved

reports.text:
SPECIMENS: (A) Right upper lobe mass, EBUS-guided FNA. (B) Mediastinal lymph node, EBUS-guided FNA.
MICROSCOPIC: Both specimens contain malignant epithelial cells in cohesive groups, without features of small cell carcinoma. Material is limited for further subtyping.
reports.conclusion: A and B: Non-small cell carcinoma, consistent with primary lung carcinoma.

documents.title: Surgical pathology, EBUS FNA
documents.author: pathology
documents.body: Final pathology received: non-small cell carcinoma in the right upper lobe mass and in the mediastinal lymph node. Routed to PCP.

documents.title: Pathology result
documents.author: PCP
documents.body: Pulmonology already told him this afternoon. I called after. Non-small cell lung cancer, involving the nodes in the middle of the chest. Staging scans (PET, brain MRI) ordered by pulmonology; oncology referral made by them. He was steady on the phone, sister there with him. Booked to see me after the oncology visit. Problem list updated.

reports.text:
FDG PET-CT from skull base to mid-thigh.
The right upper lobe mass is FDG avid. FDG-avid ipsilateral mediastinal lymph nodes. No FDG-avid contralateral mediastinal or supraclavicular nodes. No FDG-avid lesions in the liver, adrenal glands or skeleton. The 6 mm right lower lobe nodule is below PET resolution.
reports.conclusion: FDG-avid right upper lobe mass with ipsilateral mediastinal nodal disease. No distant metastatic disease.

documents.title: PET-CT
documents.author: radiology
documents.body: PET-CT report received. Disease limited to the right upper lobe mass and ipsilateral mediastinal nodes; no distant spread.

reports.study: MRI brain with and without contrast
reports.text: Multiplanar multisequence MRI of the brain before and after gadolinium. No enhancing lesion. No mass effect, hemorrhage or acute infarct. Ventricles normal in size.
reports.conclusion: No evidence of intracranial metastatic disease.

documents.author: radiology

events.reason: New diagnosis non-small cell lung cancer

documents.title: Medical oncology consultation
documents.author: oncology
documents.body:
THORACIC ONCOLOGY - NEW PATIENT CONSULTATION
Date of visit: 10/22/2024

47-year-old construction worker, ~30 pack-year current smoker with COPD, referred by pulmonology for newly diagnosed non-small cell lung cancer. Presented with 3 months of dry cough and 15 lb weight loss. CT 10/01: 4 cm RUL mass with mediastinal adenopathy. EBUS-FNA 10/09: non-small cell carcinoma in the mass and a mediastinal node. PET-CT 10/16: ipsilateral mediastinal nodal disease, no distant disease. Brain MRI 10/18: negative.

Meds: tiotropium, albuterol prn. Allergies: none known.
Family: father COPD; paternal uncle lung cancer.

Exam: thin, ECOG 1. Decreased breath sounds right upper lung field. No adenopathy. No edema.

Stage: IIIA (cT2a N2 M0).
Discussed at thoracic tumor board 10/21: N2 disease, not a surgical candidate up front.

Plan:
- Definitive concurrent chemoradiation: carboplatin AUC 2 and paclitaxel 45 mg/m2 weekly with radiation 60 Gy in 30 fractions, starting 11/04.
- If no progression after chemoradiation, consolidation durvalumab for 12 months.
- Smoking cessation strongly advised; improves outcomes during radiation.
- Radiation oncology simulation this week.

cc: primary care, pulmonology

procedures.procedure: Office visit, established patient, moderate MDM

documents.title: Office Visit - new lung cancer
documents.author: PCP
documents.body:
Came in with his sister to go over everything after seeing oncology Tuesday.

S: Stage IIIA non-small cell lung cancer, right upper lobe with mediastinal nodes, no distant spread on PET or brain MRI. Plan is chemo + radiation together starting 11/4, then an immunotherapy drug for a year. Cough the same, weight holding. Smoking down to a few a day. Mood: 'scared, but I'd rather know.' Sleep ok. No SI.

O: Vitals as charted. Tired-appearing but engaged. Lungs: decreased breath sounds right upper chest, no wheeze. Heart regular. No edema.

A/P
1. NSCLC stage IIIA - oncology/radiation oncology leading. Reviewed the plan with him and his sister, answered questions about side effects. He knows he can text me through treatment.
2. Tobacco: down to a few a day. Offered nicotine patch and varenicline again - wants to finish quitting on his own. Encouraged.
3. COPD: stable, continue tiotropium/albuterol.
4. Mood: understandable stress; PHQ-2 2. Will check in.
5. Flu and updated COVID vaccine today, before chemo starts.
Follow up after chemoradiation.

documents.title: Radiation oncology treatment summary
documents.author: radiation oncology
documents.body:
RADIATION ONCOLOGY - END OF TREATMENT SUMMARY
Treatment dates: 11/04/2024 - 12/13/2024
Diagnosis: non-small cell lung carcinoma, right upper lobe, stage IIIA (cT2a N2 M0).
Treatment: 60 Gy in 30 fractions to the right upper lobe primary and involved mediastinal nodes, with concurrent weekly carboplatin AUC 2 and paclitaxel 45 mg/m2 given by medical oncology.
Course: completed all 30 fractions and all weekly chemotherapy doses. No treatment breaks.
Follow-up: CT chest about 4 weeks after completion; medical oncology to start consolidation durvalumab if no progression.

documents.title: Oncology progress note
documents.author: oncology
documents.body:
THORACIC ONCOLOGY - FOLLOW-UP
Date of visit: 01/13/2025
Stage IIIA NSCLC, RUL, s/p concurrent chemoradiation (carboplatin/paclitaxel weekly + 60 Gy) completed 12/13/2024.
Post-treatment CT 01/08: RUL mass 2.3 cm, nodes decreased, no new disease.
Fatigue improving. Cough unchanged. Eating better.
Plan: start durvalumab 1500 mg IV every 4 weeks today, for 12 months. Discussed immune side effects - cough or breathlessness (pneumonitis), diarrhea, rash, thyroid changes - and to call for any of them. Surveillance CT every 3 months.
cc: primary care

documents.title: Office Visit - after chemoradiation
documents.author: PCP
documents.body:
S: Finished chemo/radiation 12/13. Tired, naps most afternoons, improving week by week. First durvalumab dose 1/13, no issues so far. Cough about the same, no blood. Eating more. Breathing at baseline, albuterol a few times a week. Still sneaking 3-4 cigarettes a day - embarrassed about it.
O: Weight 74 kg (about 78 in October). Vitals otherwise as charted. Lungs: no wheeze, no crackles. Heart regular. No edema.
A/P
1. NSCLC IIIA, good response on CT 1/8 (2.3 cm). On durvalumab q4 weeks via oncology. Reviewed which symptoms should prompt a call to them (new cough or shortness of breath, diarrhea, rash).
2. Tobacco: a few a day. No judgment; offered patch again - wants to keep tapering on his own.
3. COPD: stable.
4. Fatigue: expected after treatment; oncology following counts.
RTC spring.

EMERGENCY DEPARTMENT RECORD - received 09/19/2025
Date of visit: 09/14/2025

HPI: 48M with COPD and stage III non-small cell lung cancer on durvalumab, here with two days of increasing breathlessness and cough productive of green sputum.
Meds: tiotropium, albuterol inhalers; durvalumab every 4 weeks (oncology).

Family: father COPD; paternal uncle lung cancer.
Social: smoker, 30 pack-years.

Triage: RR 22, SpO2 88% on room air.
Exam: tachypneic, diffuse expiratory wheezes throughout.
ABG: pH 7.32, PaCO2 55, PaO2 70.
CXR: bronchial wall thickening, no consolidation.

Disposition: admitted to medicine.

documents.author: hospital medicine
documents.body:
DISCHARGE SUMMARY - received 09/19/2025
Admitted 09/14/2025, discharged 09/17/2025.
Principal diagnosis: acute exacerbation of COPD.
Other: stage IIIA NSCLC on consolidation durvalumab; tobacco use.

Course: admitted from the ED with hypercapnic exacerbation. Noninvasive ventilation overnight on admission, then nasal cannula; back on room air by the second hospital day. Treated with scheduled nebulized albuterol/ipratropium, prednisone 40 mg daily (5-day course) and azithromycin (5-day course). Chest imaging without consolidation; the team did not find evidence of pneumonitis. Oncology aware.

Discharge medications: tiotropium 18 mcg daily; albuterol HFA as needed; prednisone 40 mg daily to complete 5 days (last dose 09/18); azithromycin to complete 5 days (last dose 09/18).
Allergies: none known.
Follow-up: primary care in 1-2 weeks; oncology as scheduled. Smoking cessation advised.
cc: primary care

Offered a follow-up visit this week or next - he'd rather wait, sees oncology on the 13th and says he's 'had enough appointments.' Advised to call or text for any worsening. Routed to PCP.

EMERGENCY DEPARTMENT RECORD - received 04/06/2026
Date of visit: 03/28/2026

HPI: 49M with COPD, tobacco use and stage IIIA NSCLC treated with chemoradiation and durvalumab (completed 12/2025), brought in by his sister. Over the past week he has become more confused and sluggish and has hardly been eating. She says he has dropped close to 7 kg in two months and has had an ongoing cough with occasional streaks of blood.
Meds: tiotropium, albuterol.
Allergies: NKDA.
Family: father COPD; paternal uncle lung cancer.
Social: 30 pack-year smoker.

Vitals: BP 116/74, HR 84.
Exam: drowsy, oriented to name only. Moist mucous membranes. No peripheral edema. Lungs without crackles. No focal motor deficit.
Labs: Na 117, serum osm 247, urine osm 486, urine Na 58, K 3.9, creatinine 0.7, glucose 104, TSH 1.9. Hgb 12.6.
CT head: no acute abnormality.
CT chest: central RUL mass 5.8 cm, larger than in October, with enlarged mediastinal nodes.

Impression: severe hypotonic hyponatremia from SIADH, in the setting of progressive lung cancer. Euvolemic.
Plan: fluid restriction, admit to medicine with frequent sodium checks.

procedures.procedure: Hospital discharge day management, 30 minutes or less

documents.title: Hospital discharge summary
documents.author: hospital medicine
documents.body:
DISCHARGE SUMMARY - received 04/06/2026
Admitted 03/28/2026, discharged 04/02/2026.
Principal diagnosis: hyponatremia due to SIADH.
Secondary: progression of stage IIIA non-small cell lung cancer, right upper lobe; COPD; tobacco use.

Course: presented confused with Na 117, low serum osmolality, concentrated urine and high urine sodium while clinically euvolemic; TSH 1.9 and AM cortisol 17, both normal. Managed with fluid restriction to 1 L/day and sodium chloride 1 g tablets three times daily, correcting slowly. Sodium 128 on day of discharge; mentation back to his baseline by day 3. Blood-streaked sputum only, hemoglobin stable at 12.6. CT chest showed growth of the central RUL mass to 5.8 cm with enlarged mediastinal nodes. Oncology consulted: progression after chemoradiation and durvalumab; plan second-line systemic therapy as an outpatient.

Discharge medications: tiotropium 18 mcg daily; albuterol HFA as needed; sodium chloride 1 g by mouth three times daily. Fluid restriction 1 L/day.
Allergies: none known.
Follow-up: oncology next week with BMP; primary care.
cc: primary care

documents.body: Hospital records received and reviewed: SIADH with Na 117, progression of the RUL cancer. Discharged on fluid restriction and salt tabs, oncology starting second-line treatment. Asked front desk to reach out to him about coming in.

documents.title: Hospital
documents.author: patient
documents.body: Hi, wanted to let you know I was in the hospital last week, my sodium was really low and I was out of it. Cancer grew back. Starting new chemo next week with oncology. I'm ok, my sister is staying with me for a bit. Is it ok to keep using my inhalers the same?

documents.title: RE: Hospital
documents.author: PCP
documents.body: Derek, thank you for telling me - I read the hospital records and I'm sorry this came back. Yes, keep both inhalers exactly as before. Stick with the 1 liter fluid limit and the salt tablets until oncology changes them, and get your blood checks with them. I'd like to see you once treatment is underway - the front desk will reach out, or text me a time that works.
